headline: Solomon Islands signs a security treaty with Australia

sources.title: Solomon Islands ends controversial security pact with China for Australian treaty (BBC News)
Australia signs 'historic' pact with Solomon Islands in blow to China (ABC News Australia)
Signing of the Australia-Solomon Islands Treaty (Prime Minister of Australia)

chunks.text: On November 25, 2026, Solomon Islands signed a [[security treaty]] with Australia. A treaty is a [[formal agreement]] between countries. Solomon Islands is an [[island nation]] in the South Pacific. Its prime minister took about two dozen [[lawmakers]] to Australia's capital for the signing. The treaty {{grew out of}} talks in June 2026, when he visited Australia. It {{lays out}} Australian help with police, [[border protection]], schools and jobs.

verbs.correct: To begin as a result of something
verbs.wrong: To be signed by many people
verbs.why: Many small companies grow out of a simple idea. Some close friendships grow out of a shared class at school. The treaty grew out of talks in June 2026.

verbs.correct: To explain the parts of a plan
verbs.wrong: To keep a record of talks
verbs.why: The coach lays out the plan before every game. A good teacher lays out the plan for the year on the first day. The treaty lays out Australian help with police, border protection, schools and jobs.

chunks.text: A day earlier, Australian media reported on Solomon Islands' 2022 [[security pact]], or agreement, with China. They said Solomon Islands had told China it would {{pull out}} of the pact. The pact, signed by a former prime minister, let China {{send in}} police teams. It was never [[made public]]. It {{stirred up}} [[fears]] in Australia and the U.S. that China wanted a [[foothold]], a starting point for power, in the Pacific.

verbs.why: Some players pull out of a contract early. A country sometimes pulls out of a trade deal after an election. Reports said Solomon Islands had told China it would pull out of the 2022 pact.

verbs.correct: To send officers to a place
verbs.why: The city sends in extra police after a big storm. The government sends in soldiers when a flood hits. The 2022 pact let China send in police teams to Solomon Islands.
A rude post online often stirs up anger. Rumors about job cuts stir up fear at work. The 2022 pact stirred up fears in Australia and the U.S.

chunks.text: The China pact was set to {{run out}} in April 2027. Reports said the country would not [[renew]] it, or make it last longer. The new treaty {{rules out}} any foreign [[military base]] there. Solomon Islands will first ask members of the Pacific Islands Forum for [[security help]]. This group of Pacific nations includes Australia but not China. Australia will help {{build up}} the country's [[police force]]. It will also {{step up}} support for [[free education]].

verbs.correct: To end at a set time
verbs.why: My phone contract runs out in March. The free trial runs out after thirty days. The China pact was set to run out in April 2027.

verbs.correct: To say something will not happen
verbs.why: The coach rules out any changes to the team before the final. The company rules out job cuts for the rest of the year. The new treaty rules out any foreign military base in Solomon Islands.

verbs.wrong: To swear an oath of office
verbs.why: Daily exercise builds up your heart. Reading every night builds up a child's language skills. Australia will help build up the police force in Solomon Islands.
Stores step up their hiring before the busy season. The city steps up bus service during big games. Australia will step up support for free education in Solomon Islands.

chunks.text: Australia will {{open up}} jobs in Australia for Solomon Islanders in [[child care]] and care for older people. Solomon Islands' prime minister {{held back}} [[details]] about the China pact. He said a [[secrecy clause]] keeps it private. China's foreign ministry did not confirm or deny the reports. The former prime minister who signed that pact now leads the [[opposition]], the parties not in power. He {{spoke out}} against ending it. The current prime minister {{brushed off}} the risk of a vote to remove him.

verbs.why: A new factory opens up hundreds of jobs in a small town. Free classes open up new chances for adults. Australia will open up more jobs in Australia for Solomon Islanders in child care.

verbs.wrong: To sign a document in public
verbs.why: Some patients hold back details from their doctor. Police often hold back the names of people in a crash. Solomon Islands' prime minister held back details about the China pact.

verbs.wrong: To study a report for years
verbs.why: Many parents speak out when a school closes. Some workers speak out about unsafe jobs. The opposition leader spoke out against ending the pact with China.
My brother brushes off every cold and goes to work. Some players brush off bad news about their team. The current prime minister brushed off the risk of a vote to remove him.

mainIdea.s: Solomon Islands signed a security treaty with Australia that bans foreign military bases. Reports said it would leave its 2022 China pact, but its leader did not confirm it.
mainIdea.why: The treaty rules out any foreign military base there. Australian media reported the plan to pull out of the China pact, and its leader held back details.

mainIdea.s: Solomon Islands openly announced the end of its police deal with China at a signing with Australia. China's government confirmed the news and said it was very unhappy.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the prime minister held back details about the China pact. China's foreign ministry did not confirm or deny the reports.

mainIdea.s: A strong storm hit Solomon Islands and damaged many roads and homes in the countryside. Australia sent food and water, and its army helped rebuild several schools there.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a security treaty. Solomon Islands signed it with Australia, and Australia will help build up its police force.

lines.text: Did you see that Solomon Islands signed a security treaty with Australia?
I did. Where is Solomon Islands, exactly?
It's an island nation in the South Pacific. Its prime minister, Matthew Wale, took about two dozen lawmakers with him for the signing.
What does the treaty actually say?
It {{lays out}} help with police, border protection, schools and jobs. It also {{rules out}} any foreign military base there.
Well, in 2022, Solomon Islands signed a pact that let China {{send in}} police teams. The full text stayed [[under wraps]].
I remember. That deal {{stirred up}} a lot of fear in Australia and the U.S.
Right. Now Australian media say Solomon Islands told China it will {{pull out}}. The pact {{runs out}} in April 2027, and they say it won't be renewed.
Did the prime minister confirm that?
No. He was pretty [[tight-lipped]]. He {{held back}} details and said the China pact has a secrecy clause.
So we still don't have [[the full picture]].
Pretty much. China's foreign ministry didn't confirm or deny it either.
What does Solomon Islands get from Australia?
Australia will help {{build up}} its police force and {{open up}} jobs in Australia in child care. It will also {{step up}} its support for free education.
Is everyone in Solomon Islands [[on board]] with the deal?
Not everyone. The opposition leader {{spoke out}} against ending the China pact.
And Wale just {{brushed off}} the risk of a vote against him? He sounds confident.
